page: Vultr vhp-12c-24gb-amd is a High Performance family server featuring 12 shared vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC processor running at 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The hardware configuration includes 6 physical cores with 2 threads per core, 24.0 GB of system memory providing 2.0 GB per core, and a bundled 500 GB NVMe SSD for local storage. No GPU is included in this configuration.

Benchmark data indicates average performance across most multi-core and single-core compute tasks. The server achieved a Geekbench single-core score of 1233.0 and a multi-core score of 7655.0, alongside a PassMark CPU score of 17153.85. However, single-threaded operations show notable performance bottlenecks, with gzip compression and bzip3 decompression scoring in the bottom 10%. Memory performance is also a relative weakness, with the PassMark memory score falling into the bottom 25%, though cached small-block read bandwidth remains high at 1019.76 GB/sec.

Given the shared CPU allocation and the 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, this server offers a cost-efficient option for multi-threaded workloads that do not require dedicated CPU cores. It is well-suited for static web serving, database operations, and software compilation, as demonstrated by its average performance in Redis SET operations and Geekbench clang compilation. It is less suitable for memory-intensive applications or single-threaded compression tasks due to documented performance limitations in those areas.
description: The Vultr vhp-12c-24gb-amd is an x86_64 High Performance server configured with 12 shared AMD EPYC vCPUs, 24.0 GB of RAM, and a 500 GB NVMe SSD. It delivers average multi-core performance, as evidenced by a Geekbench multi-core score of 7655.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 17153.85. However, it exhibits performance trade-offs, particularly in single-threaded tasks like gzip compression and memory-intensive operations, which rank in the lower percentiles. With a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and shared CPU resources, this instance provides a cost-effective platform for parallelized workloads. It is best suited for multi-threaded applications, static web serving, software compilation, and moderate database operations that can leverage its 12 vCPUs without requiring dedicated hardware threads.
